answer: New identities should start with a low emission limit, rising only when unrelated peers verify random work samples from signed records. Cluster identities that recycle evidence or share endorsers and limit each cluster to one participant's reward cap. For instance, cross-check a nadir temperature against a device log, verify opal provenance with a lab certificate, or compare zephyr wind reports with timestamped station records. An attacker needs distinct, auditable evidence and separate reviewers; adding keys alone earns nothing.
